title: Collect the Most Treasure on a One-Way Tour

concept.title: Shrink every cycle group to one node: the graph becomes acyclic and a simple DP works
body: Each node has a treasure value. You start at any node and walk along the edges; you may visit nodes again, but a node's treasure counts **only once**. What is the largest total treasure you can collect? If the graph has cycles, you can go round a cycle and collect **all** its treasures, and then leave. In fact, inside a strongly connected component you can visit all of its nodes before leaving.

So replace every strongly connected component by a single node whose value is the **sum of the values of its nodes**. The new graph, the *condensation*, has no cycle, and the problem becomes the "heaviest path in a DAG" task: `best[c]` = the largest total of a path that ends in the component `c`. Process the components in a topological order: the Kosaraju numbering already gives one (sources first). A component `c` passes `best[c]` on to every component `d` that it has an edge to: `best[d] = max(best[d], best[c] + value[d])`.
The answer can reach 2 * 10^13 (20000 values of 10^9), so 64-bit integers are needed. The time is O(n + m).

statement: A directed graph has `n` nodes with treasure values and `m` edges. You choose a starting node and walk along edges as far as you like; you may visit a node many times, but its treasure is collected only once. Print the largest total treasure you can collect.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers: the value of every node.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge from `u` to `v`.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: The nodes 1 and 2 form a cycle (1 + 2 = 3). The best tour is 1, 2, 3, 4 with 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10; going to node 5 instead gives 1 + 2 + 5 = 8.

hints: Find the strongly connected components and add up the values inside each.
The components are numbered in topological order; process them in that order.
Pass the best total from a component to the components it points to, and print the largest value.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
value = list(map(int, input().split()))
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

explanation: Strongly connected components are found and their values summed; processing the components in topological order, each component offers its best total to the components it points to. The answer is the largest total of any component.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).
